findings.explanation: docs/runbooks/admin-auth-rbac-audit-runbook.md:22 describes the `maintainer` role as "support plus export and audit read" (read-only), and lines 25-27 of the same doc state: "Write permissions are present only as future gates. They must not be connected to production write routes until the write workflow has its own design, confirmation UI, tests, and owner approval." But core/admin-auth.js:25-33 actually grants `maintainer` both PERMISSIONS.INTERNAL_NOTE_WRITE (line 31) and PERMISSIONS.PRODUCT_WRITE (line 32) — permissions that are themselves classified as write permissions in the WRITE_PERMISSIONS set at admin-auth.js:37-42. The role's real capability (write access) is not reflected in the doc's role summary.

docs/runbooks/admin-auth-rbac-audit-runbook.md:25-27 claims write permissions "are present only as future gates" and "must not be connected to production write routes" until a separate write workflow is designed and approved. Contrary to that, core/admin-routes.js:1382-1389 (`createShopApi`, the live shop-creation endpoint) already calls `authorizeAdminRequest` with `permission: PERMISSIONS.PRODUCT_WRITE` (line 1384), and dozens of other routes in the same file (e.g. lines 1373, 1405, 1436, 1459 ...) do the same. Since `maintainer` (and `owner`) already hold PRODUCT_WRITE per core/admin-auth.js:32/34, these write routes are already reachable in production today, not gated behind future approval as the runbook states.
